title: Le Blanc's objections to Valencia
source_text: CXLV. In ejus vero sententia hoc peculiare incommodum occurrit, quod quae de gratia efficaci dicit, in sola peccatoris ad Deum conversione locum habere possint, non vero in bonis operibus hominis jam conversi; ad quae nulla requiritur nova habitualis gratiae infusio, & ad quae tamen gratia efficax se extendit. Ac praeterea mihi quidem intelligibile non est, quomodo infusio gratiae habitualis possit esse hominis conversione prior in genere causae efficientis, & simul tamen eadem conversione posterior in genere causae dispositivae.
pass_a_gloss: CXLV. But in his opinion this peculiar difficulty occurs, that what he says of efficacious grace, can have place only in the conversion of the sinner to God, but not in the good works of a man already converted; for which no new infusion of habitual grace is required, & to which nevertheless efficacious grace extends itself. And besides to me indeed it is not intelligible, how the infusion of habitual grace can be prior to the man's conversion in the genus of efficient cause, & at the same time nevertheless posterior to the same conversion in the genus of dispositive cause.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXLV. His opinion runs into a difficulty of its own: what he says about efficacious grace can apply only to the sinner's conversion to God, not to the good works of someone already converted. Those works need no new infusion of habitual grace, and yet efficacious grace extends to them as well.

Besides, for my part I cannot understand how the infusion of habitual grace can be prior to a person's conversion as efficient cause and yet at the same time posterior to that same conversion as dispositive cause.
